title: Why 24-bit colour means 16.7 million colours
summary: 24 bits split into 8 each for red, green and blue. 256 × 256 × 256 is 16,777,216 colours, the same as 2 to the power 24.

beats.say: A twenty four bit pixel can show sixteen million colors.
Twenty four bits split evenly into red, green and blue.
That is eight bits for each color channel.
Eight bits can hold two hundred fifty six different values.
So each channel runs from zero to two fifty five.
Red, green and blue each pick one of those values.
Same number as two to the power of twenty four.
Thirty two bit color usually adds eight bits for transparency, not more colors.
Sixteen million colors is arithmetic on bits.
Add bits, and the count of colors multiplies.

claims.note: Wikipedia, Color depth: almost all cases of 32 bits per pixel assign 24 bits to the color and the remaining 8 to alpha or leave them unused

facts.claim: 24-bit color almost always uses 8 bits each for red, green and blue, giving 2^24 = 16,777,216 color variations
facts.note: Wikipedia, Color depth: '24 bits almost always use 8 bits each of R, G, and B'; 2^24 gives 16,777,216 color variations

facts.claim: 32 bits per pixel usually assigns 24 bits to color and 8 to the alpha channel (transparency) or leaves them unused
8 bits allow 2^8 = 256 combinations per channel, and three 8-bit channels give 16,777,216 colors
facts.note: Cambridge in Colour, Bit depth tutorial: 8 bits give 256 values per primary; three channels give as many as 16,777,216 colors, called true color
